quizzes.stem: A team hand-writes a client in a language that has no SDK. The request carries the content type and the key, and the body copies the documentation's example, yet every call fails with a 400. Which addition is most likely missing?

options.a: The version header that names the API revision in use by the caller
options.b: An accept header that names the media type the client wants back
options.c: A user-agent header that names the client library and its version
options.d: A workspace header that names the workspace this call should run under

explanation.a: The overview lists the version header as required, and a hand-written client has to send it itself.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Authentication, version and body type are all a plain request needs", and the media type of the reply is not among them.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the overview marks no Accept or User-Agent header as required", and the SDKs add that header for their own sake.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the workspace header is needed "only when the key spans several workspaces".

quizzes.stem: A gateway between a service and the provider starts answering some failures with web pages. The service's failure handler throws while decoding them. Which design is best?

options.a: Decode the body as JSON first and stop the process whenever that decoding fails
options.b: Ask the gateway team to promise that every reply stays JSON in the provider's own format
options.c: Map each non-2xx status to a typed fault, using the raw text if the body is not JSON
options.d: Retry each failing call until the body decodes cleanly into the expected shape

explanation.c: A hand-written client has to cope with a non-JSON body, so the handler falls back to the text.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "always JSON is the API's promise about its own errors", and a gateway is not covered by it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a hand-written client must keep working when the body is HTML".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the proxy answers the same page again".

quizzes.stem: Verbose diagnostics are on in a deployed service. Credentials look masked in the output, but customers' messages show up in it. What should the team do?

options.a: Keep it on, because the SDK masks sensitive data in request and response bodies
options.b: Switch that mode off for live traffic so that request bodies stay out of it
options.c: Redact the headers further so that the output holds no credentials at all
options.d: Log only the failing calls so that less customer text reaches the output

explanation.b: In that mode "all HTTP requests and responses are logged, including headers and bodies", so it does not belong on live traffic, where those bodies are customer text.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "sensitive data in request and response bodies may still be visible".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "headers are partly redacted, bodies are not", and the leak is in the bodies.
explanation.d: Ruled out because failing calls carry customer text too, and "customer text does not belong in a log by default".

quizzes.stem: A service sets nothing on its SDK client and calls the API in a month where the organisation has already reached its monthly spend cap. What happens to each call?

options.a: It is attempted once, because the SDK reads the cap and stops early
options.b: It is attempted once, because a 429 is never retried by the SDK
options.c: It is attempted three times, and the third attempt succeeds after a pause
options.d: It is attempted three times in all, and every one of the attempts fails

explanation.d: Two retries after the first attempt make three, and for a spend-cap 429 "every retry of it fails".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a spend-cap 429 is retried, and "module 15 shows the SDK retrying one".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the cap "stays in force until the next month begins", so no pause helps.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the retry default "applies to every retryable failure, including ones that cannot succeed", and the SDK does not inspect the cap.

quizzes.stem: A team's report generator sets a very large `max_tokens` on a non-streaming call and now fails intermittently on the office network after several minutes without any reply. Which change is best?

options.a: Open a websocket so that the server can push the report when it is ready
options.b: Use server-sent events so that data arrives while the text is written
options.c: Raise the client timeout so that the call may stay silent for longer
options.d: Split the report into three prompts and send them over three connections

explanation.b: Streaming keeps data moving: "Bytes keep flowing, and the connection is not idle".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "there is no client-to-server traffic to carry" in a model call, and a websocket is "not what the API sends".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Some networks may drop idle connections after a variable period of time", so a longer timeout on your side does not help.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Streaming or a batch is the documented fix", and three non-streaming calls are each still silent while they are generated.

quizzes.stem: A developer proposes a websocket between a web page and the model API so that the page can send a stop signal during a long answer. Which design is best?

options.a: Send a second HTTP request that tells the model to stop generating
options.b: Send the stop signal as an event on the open stream of the reply
options.c: Switch to the websocket, because only that protocol allows a cancel
options.d: Keep the stream and close the connection when the user wants it to end

explanation.d: The stream runs on one ordinary HTTP request, and the client cancels "by closing the connection".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the stream is one-directional: "after the request is sent, the client only listens".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a websocket adds an upgrade, a session to restore and trouble at every proxy, and gives nothing in return".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page documents "breaking out of the loop or calling stream.controller.abort()", not a second request.

quizzes.stem: A hand-written client and an SDK client call the API from the same service. After the provider adds a new stop reason value, only the hand-written client starts failing. Which cause is most likely?

options.a: It has no retries, which the SDK would have supplied automatically
options.b: Its logic assumes that the set of labels it saw is complete
options.c: It lacks the identifying platform headers that the SDK sends
options.d: It was written against an older revision of the contract header

explanation.b: A client that fails on an unknown value breaks "on a change the versioning page allows", and the page says a stop reason is among the values "you do not know" that must be tolerated, not only a field.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the new value arrives in a 200, and "a successful reply is a JSON object", so there is no error for a retry to repeat.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the SDK's extra headers "help debugging and are not part of your contract".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the only current value of anthropic-version is 2023-06-01", and an older one "may be unavailable for new users".

quizzes.stem: A service builds a new SDK client for every streamed call, and its latency and open-socket count grow under load. Which change is best?

options.a: Make one instance at start-up so that each handler reuses its pool
options.b: Move the calls to a websocket so that one connection is kept open
options.c: Turn streaming off so that fewer sockets are used by each of the calls
options.d: Raise the output limit so that fewer calls are needed for the same work

explanation.a: The page says to reuse connections, because each client "has a connection pool and thread pools that are better shared".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a websocket adds an upgrade, a session to restore and trouble at every proxy, and gives nothing in return".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the sockets come from the clients, not from streaming: "a new client means a new connection pool each time".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the cost shows up as latency and sockets" and comes from the number of clients, which the output limit does not change.

quizzes.stem: A call that asks for incremental output returns 200 and a few events, and then the network drops. A developer records the call as successful because of the 200. What should the page's reader tell them?

options.a: The code shows only that the reply began, so the end must be checked as well
options.b: The code is final, since the server sends it after the whole message is written
options.c: The events already received form a complete message and can be stored as the result
options.d: The stream resumes from its last event on reconnect, so the call will still finish

explanation.a: "A streamed reply can start with a 200 and still end with an error event", so the 200 shows only that the reply began and the end of the stream has to be checked as well.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the server answers with a normal HTTP response whose body is a stream", so the status comes before the message is written.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the connection stays open until the message is complete", and this one dropped before it was.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a reconnect for server-sent events means "Start a new request", not a resumed stream.

quizzes.stem: A team logs every failing call so that it can open tickets with the provider's support. Which record should the service keep for each call?

options.a: The authorization header and the body, so that the call can be reproduced
options.b: The complete request and reply, so that support staff can replay them
options.c: The request id, the status and the error type, so staff can locate it
options.d: Only the time of the call, since the provider can find the call from it

explanation.c: The request id is what support asks for: "include it when you contact support about a specific request", and the status and type classify the failure without carrying a key or customer text.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "customer text does not belong in a log by default".
explanation.a: Ruled out because an error message that is logged "is read by people who must not see a key", and a header would carry the key.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the request id is "a globally unique identifier for the request", and a time stamp does not single out one call.
